Benchmark: supplementary checks

Source: vignettes/articles/benchmark-supplement.qmd

The report’s Benchmarking section compares the required quantities of the project description: the coefficients, their standard errors, theta (NB) or log(theta) (ZINB), and the log-likelihood, each with a pass/fail tolerance. This article adds comparisons that are not graded requirements, so they have no tolerances. They are shown with two measures of difference:

  • the absolute difference |ours − reference|, the measure the requirements use;
  • the relative difference |ours − reference| / |reference|, which puts quantities of different sizes on a common footing (a relative difference of 1e-5 means agreement to about five significant digits).

The data, formulas and settings are those of the report: our functions at their default settings, MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl() with tight tolerances.

Standard errors of theta and log(theta)

nbreg() reports SE(theta) and zinbreg() reports SE(log theta), as the references do. Their agreement with the references:

ZINB with the numeric Hessian

zinbreg() computes standard errors from the analytic Hessian (matrix of second derivatives) of the log-likelihood by default; with zinbreg_control(hessian = "numeric") it differentiates the log-likelihood numerically instead (numDeriv::hessian()). The option only changes how the matrix used for the standard errors is computed: the EM iterations and the gradient check that stops them are the same, so the estimates are identical and this checks the standard errors by a second, independent route.

Our two Hessian methods give standard errors that agree with each other to 2.47e-07, far more closely than either agrees with zeroinfl() (at least 6.38e-06). The remaining differences from zeroinfl() therefore come from the small differences between the two packages’ estimates, not from how the standard errors are computed.

Validity checks

Every comparison in the report and here is made only after these checks pass for both fits of a pair. A failed check would be reported here with its reason, and the comparison would be marked as not assessed.

Timing with the numeric Hessian

The numeric Hessian needs many more evaluations of the log-likelihood, so it is slower. Timings are from the saved benchmark results (median of 10 runs, with the range).

The installed package’s code fingerprint (f6f29a27eff95d07ab6302d5a428954e) matches the code that produced the timings (commit 65f2720b0fc178074ae477c7b23d55ba54768b71).
